summary: Standardize Support incident response macros to match SRE status-page update templates
description:
Background
Support is repeatedly fielding tickets where the customer asks “what’s impacted?” during incidents and we don’t have consistent language aligned with SRE’s status-page updates. This creates back-and-forth and increases risk of contradictory external comms.

Request
Create standardized Support macros/templates that:
- Match SRE’s incident phases (Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved)
- Use the same customer-impact language (degraded performance vs partial outage) and component naming
- Provide copy-ready “what you can do now” guidance (retry/backoff, fallback models, region pinning) without overpromising
- Include a placeholder/link to the public status page incident and “next update” timing where available
- Respect disclosure boundaries (no customer names, no exploit-like detail, no vendor blame specifics)

Where these will be used
- Internal responses in Jira comments for Support-owned tickets during incidents
- Customer emails for enterprise escalations (CSMs/AEs may reuse)
- Internal notes for consistent updates until SRE publishes on status page

Proposed deliverables
1) Macro set (4 phases + a “post-incident summary request” macro)
2) Short usage guidance (when to use each macro, what fields to fill in, what not to say)
3) Alignment review with SRE oncall lead + Security/Compliance for disclosure guardrails

Acceptance criteria
- Macro text approved by SRE sponsor (Sean Gallagher) or SRE delivery lead (Rafael Mendes)
- Includes explicit placeholders for: impacted components, regions, customer impact, mitigation/workaround, next update time
- Links to the canonical Confluence template page and disclosure policy
- Shared with Support team (announcement + pinned in #support)

Notes
- Please keep macros short; customers skim. A second paragraph is fine only if it contains a concrete action.
- Many of our issues are partial (e.g., streaming-only disconnects) — we need language that doesn’t imply full outage.
customer_impact: Internal efficiency + consistency risk: inconsistent comms during incidents leading to longer tickets, escalations, and conflicting statements vs status page.
comments:
2024-06-24 - Dev Patel (Reporter)
We need these macros ASAP. In the last two incidents we had three separate wording variants for “degraded streaming” and one rep wrote “outage” while status said “degraded performance.” I’m linking SUP-18421 as the latest example.

Ideal format: short macro with bracketed placeholders and a line that says “We will post another update by <time>” when SRE has provided one.
2024-06-25 - Owen Phillips
+1. Also add a macro for “we’re seeing elevated 429s / capacity constraints” that explains backoff + optionally switching regions/models if the customer has that configured.
2024-06-26 - Kira Thompson (Assignee)
Drafted macro set v0.1 and shared in #support for feedback. Question for SRE: should we say “partial outage” or “degraded performance” when only a subset of requests fail (e.g., streaming disconnects) but non-streaming completions are fine?
2024-06-26 - Rafael Mendes
Use “degraded performance” when the service is still operating but with elevated errors/latency for a subset. Use “partial outage” when the impact is clearly preventing a meaningful portion of customers from using a specific product surface (e.g., embeddings requests failing broadly in a region). Support macros should mirror the status page language and include the component name.

Also: avoid “root cause is X” until status update moves to Identified.
2024-06-27 - Dr. Aisha Rahman
Security note: macros must not include provider-specific blame or any hint of vulnerability/exploit details. “Upstream dependency degradation” is acceptable. Avoid naming specific cloud vendor services unless SRE has already publicly stated it.
2024-07-01 - Kira Thompson (Assignee)
Updated macros v0.3:
- Added explicit “If you’re seeing timeouts, try…” guidance
- Added “We’ll update again by <next_update_time>” line
- Added a “requesting post-incident summary” macro that sets expectations (summary within 3 business days for Sev1+)
Pending final review from Dev + SRE lead.
2024-07-03 - Dev Patel
Approved. Please post final links and announce in #support. Also add to onboarding checklist for new support reps.
resolution_notes:
Published Support macro set aligned to SRE incident phases and component taxonomy. Macros include placeholders for impacted components/regions, mitigation/workaround guidance, and next-update timing. Disclosure guardrails reviewed with Security.

Rollout:
- Shared final macro doc + usage guidance in #support and pinned
- Added link to Support playbook and new-hire onboarding checklist

Follow-ups:
- Revisit macro text after status page component rollout (regional components + Streaming/Embeddings/Rerank naming) to ensure exact match.
next_steps: Re-audit macros after the status page taxonomy is finalized and incident-bot guided prompts ship; ensure support macros stay consistent with any template wording changes.
